title: Statutes of limitations — five returns
instructions: Each return below is an individual Year 1 return due **April 15, Year 2**. Select the last date for the action described (assume no weekends or holidays).

rows.label: IRS assessment: return filed early on February 1, Year 2
rows.explanation: Early returns are treated as filed on the due date; 3 years from April 15, Year 2.

rows.label: IRS assessment: return filed under extension on October 10, Year 2
rows.explanation: 3 years from the actual (timely extended) filing date.

rows.label: IRS assessment: return filed April 15, Year 2, omitting 30% of gross income
rows.explanation: Omissions over 25% of gross income extend the period to 6 years.

rows.label: IRS assessment: fraudulent return
rows.explanation: Fraud keeps the assessment period open indefinitely.

rows.label: Taxpayer refund claim: return filed April 15, Year 2; additional tax paid June 1, Year 4
rows.explanation: The later of 3 years from filing or 2 years from payment.
